long_biography.plain_text:
Seattle sailor Cranston Paschall, known as Boo, helped promote a Pacific Northwest starting point for ocean racing to Hawaii. He had sailed the Swiftsure and other regional races before joining discussions with Jim Innes, Lol Killam and Ron Ramsay in 1964. Their aim was to test seamanship offshore without first taking boats south to Los Angeles for the Transpac.

A member of Seattle's sailing community, Paschall joined a group that brought together sailors from Vancouver and Victoria as well as his own city. The Victoria-Maui race first took place the following year; Innes and Killam subsequently secured joint sponsorship from clubs in Vancouver and Lahaina.
